title: a-run-stops-the-units-it-started
intention: A tester run stops every systemd user unit its subject started — any service the user manager records as handed the run's CAIRN_TESTER_TEST_ID, failed ones included — and names each in evidence 'killed', whether or not the run sits inside the seal.
why: Akien 2026-10-05 (/home/akien/.cairn/foreground-decisions.md 8e: the tester kills what the run started; 8g: the web server leak, 'as long as it gets fixed'). The lived symptom: f04d5ef26a48's seal came back red with the launcher's loop unit left running in the live user manager — inside the seal's user namespace /proc/<pid>/environ of a unit's process reads Permission denied, so bf3c16162827's kill could not see it, and a failed unit has no process for it to see anywhere.
traces_to: bf3c16162827 (a tester run owns what it started — Akien 8e, /home/akien/.cairn/foreground-decisions.md: the tester kills what the run started); Akien 8g ('the web server leak ... as long as it gets fixed'); Law 7 (a manager that cannot be asked is named in evidence, never silent); RULE 1 (the kill is the tester's, so the change lives in cairn/devices/tester)
how: cairn/devices/tester/runs.py gains stop_its_units(test): list the user manager's services, read their Environment through one `systemctl --user show`, stop and reset-failed every one carrying the id, return {unit, signal}; kill_what_it_started calls it before its /proc scan and returns both lists. Red proof cairn/devices/tester/proofs/test_a_run_stops_the_units_it_started.py on disk (1/4 at f2e9d216).
falsifier: GREEN when cairn/devices/tester/proofs/test_a_run_stops_the_units_it_started.py prints four ok lines and exits 0, bare and under the tester's seal: (1) a service the subject starts with systemd-run --setenv of the run's id is gone from the user manager after the run and evidence killed names it under unit; (2) a service carrying the id that exited 1 is gone after the run and named; (3) the same as 1 when the subject times out; (4) a service started beside the run with no id, or with another run's id, is still active afterwards; and cairn/devices/tester/proofs/test_a_first_seal_is_taken_under_the_seal.py, cairn/devices/tester/proofs/test_a_green_over_a_red_under_other_conditions_notifies.py, cairn/devices/tester/proofs/test_a_green_seal_names_a_tooth.py, cairn/devices/tester/proofs/test_a_proof_declares_its_own_time_limit.py, cairn/devices/tester/proofs/test_a_run_owns_what_it_started.py, cairn/devices/tester/proofs/test_a_seal_inside_a_seal_inherits.py, cairn/devices/tester/proofs/test_instance_seal.py, cairn/devices/tester/proofs/test_tester.py, cairn/devices/tester/proofs/test_the_tester_is_reached_only_through_its_interface.py, cairn/devices/tester/proofs/test_the_tester_takes_its_reply.py, cairn/tools/base/proofs/test_a_marked_envelope_goes_back_to_its_sender.py stay green. RED if any fails. Wrong intent if a test run must leave a unit it started alive.
watchme: none, because (cairn/devices/tester/device.py run_proof) every tester run's validation record names what its kill reached in evidence killed, now including units, so every seal counts them with no probe
children: none, because the change is one file (cairn/devices/tester/runs.py) in one component with one proof on disk (cairn/devices/tester/proofs/test_a_run_stops_the_units_it_started.py)

decisions.text: D1: SETTLED: apply exactly the unified diff carried in this ticket's build_patch field (`git apply` from a file holding that text, run in the cairn repo root). It edits only cairn/devices/tester/runs.py: adds _systemctl, _units_carrying (list-units --all --type=service, one show -p Id -p Environment, match CAIRN_TESTER_TEST_ID=<id>) and stop_its_units (stop + reset-failed each, returns {unit, signal}; a manager that cannot be asked returns one entry naming why); kill_what_it_started calls stop_its_units first and returns units + processes. No other code changes.

D2: SETTLED: the proof cairn/devices/tester/proofs/test_a_run_stops_the_units_it_started.py is already on disk, committed red at f2e9d216 (1 of 4: tooth 4 green, 1-3 red). After the build it prints four ok lines and exits 0. The regression proofs cairn/devices/tester/proofs/test_a_first_seal_is_taken_under_the_seal.py, cairn/devices/tester/proofs/test_a_green_over_a_red_under_other_conditions_notifies.py, cairn/devices/tester/proofs/test_a_green_seal_names_a_tooth.py, cairn/devices/tester/proofs/test_a_proof_declares_its_own_time_limit.py, cairn/devices/tester/proofs/test_a_run_owns_what_it_started.py, cairn/devices/tester/proofs/test_a_seal_inside_a_seal_inherits.py, cairn/devices/tester/proofs/test_instance_seal.py, cairn/devices/tester/proofs/test_tester.py, cairn/devices/tester/proofs/test_the_tester_is_reached_only_through_its_interface.py, cairn/devices/tester/proofs/test_the_tester_takes_its_reply.py, cairn/tools/base/proofs/test_a_marked_envelope_goes_back_to_its_sender.py each exit 0, run as `python3 <path>` from the cairn repo root (plain scripts with a __main__ block). cairn/devices/tester/proofs/test_isolation.py is not a gate here (red at HEAD for codemother's mail volume, gap ticket C).

--- a/cairn/devices/tester/runs.py
+++ b/cairn/devices/tester/runs.py
@@ -13,7 +13,13 @@ marks what it sends with ``testing_mark.mark(<that id>)``. Everything else hangs
     the cairn device's sleep work, so nothing here needs a sweep of its own;
   - the processes the run started: anything whose environment still carries the id after the
     subject has exited. The environment survives setsid and a timed-out parent, which a
-    process-group kill does not.
+    process-group kill does not;
+  - the systemd user units the run started: any service the manager records as handed the id.
+    /proc cannot see these in two cases (measured 2026-10-05, found by f04d5ef26a48's seal): a
+    unit that FAILED has no process left, and inside the seal's user namespace
+    /proc/<pid>/environ of every process outside it reads "Permission denied". The manager's
+    own record (``systemctl --user show -p Environment``) reads through the seal, so the run
+    asks it, stops what carries the id and clears the failed ones.
 """
 from __future__ import annotations
 
@@ -21,6 +27,7 @@ import json
 import os
 import re
 import signal
+import subprocess
 import time
 from datetime import datetime, timezone
 from pathlib import Path
@@ -95,9 +102,47 @@ def _carrying(test: str) -> list[dict]:
     return found
 
 
+def _systemctl(*argv: str) -> subprocess.CompletedProcess:
+    return subprocess.run(["systemctl", "--user", *argv], capture_output=True, text=True, timeout=30)
+
+
+def _units_carrying(test: str) -> list[str]:
+    """Every service the user manager records as handed the run's id, failed ones included."""
+    listed = _systemctl("list-units", "--all", "--no-legend", "--plain", "--type=service")
+    names = [line.split()[0] for line in listed.stdout.splitlines() if line.strip()]
+    if not names:
+        return []
+    shown = _systemctl("show", "-p", "Id", "-p", "Environment", "--", *names)
+    tag, found, unit = f"{ENV}={test}", [], None
+    for line in shown.stdout.splitlines():
+        if line.startswith("Id="):
+            unit = line[3:]
+        elif line.startswith("Environment=") and unit and tag in line[12:].split():
+            found.append(unit)
+    return found
+
+
+def stop_its_units(test: str) -> list[dict]:
+    """Stop every user service carrying the run's id and clear it from the manager. A manager
+    that cannot be asked is named in what comes back, never passed over in silence (Law 7)."""
+    try:
+        units = _units_carrying(test)
+    except (OSError, subprocess.TimeoutExpired) as exc:
+        return [{"unit": None, "signal": f"none: the user manager could not be asked: {exc}"}]
+    out = []
+    for unit in units:
+        stop = _systemctl("stop", unit)
+        _systemctl("reset-failed", unit)
+        out.append({"unit": unit, "signal": "stop" if stop.returncode == 0
+                    else f"stop failed: {stop.stderr.strip()[:200]}"})
+    return out
+
+
 def kill_what_it_started(test: str) -> list[dict]:
-    """SIGTERM every live process still carrying the run's id, SIGKILL what outlives the grace.
-    Returns what was found, each with the signal that ended it (or the error that stopped us)."""

+    it (or the error that stopped us)."""

     found = _carrying(test)
     for p in found:
         try:
@@ -117,4 +162,4 @@ def kill_what_it_started(test: str) -> list[dict]:
                 p["signal"] = "KILL"
             except OSError as exc:
